2 Helpful Objects

This section needs to be adjusted for each user. Either, have your own color scheme that matches your number of clusters, replicates, samples, age groups, and genotype groups -or- remove any specified color pallet in the graphing below.

# Color palette for PIPseq that coordinates with Yellowstone for clusters
cluster_colors<- c("#0067A2", "#CC782B", "#5A8D66", "#509EA0", "#71A2B8", "#8A9BA9", "#B46DB3", "black")

# Color palette for replicates -- adapted from the Torres colors
replicate_colors <- c( "#7391BD" ,"#894846" ,"#E9988C" ,"#535260", "#B7A7A6" ,"#785838", "#C68D61" ,"#93995C")

# Color pallete for "disordered" sample_ID (in order of lexicon, 1, 10-16, 2-9)
sample_colors_d <- c("#C00000", "#FF8082", "#BFA85F", "#CCCA79", "#799E51", "#448A64", 
  "#568BB1", "#775790", "#FF0000", "#FFC000", "#F5EF1E", "#92D050", 
  "#00B050", "#0070C0", "#7030A0", "#D08B8C")

# Group color pallet
age_colors <- c("#BFA85F", "purple")

# genotype color pallet
genotype_colors <- c("orange", "blue")

This doesn’t work! Even though I know I just ran PrepSCTFindMarkers()

Error in FindMarkers.SCTAssay(object = data.use, latent.vars = latent.vars, : Object contains multiple models with unequal library sizes. Run PrepSCTFindMarkers() before running FindMarkers().

DimPlot(SO)

# df2 <- FindMarkers(SO, ident.1 = "normal", group.by = "myelination", subset.ident = "OPC", logfc.threshold = 0.25, min.pct = 0.1)

7 Solution

I think this problem stems from multiple issues. Mostly from new Seurat behaviors in V5 vs. V4 that we’re not used to yet.

First, the RNA assay layers were never joined together, which I wonder if it messed up the initial SCT calculations. Regardless, there are multiple SCT assays in this object which I think is the heart of the problem.

So my workaround is to:
1) Set SO default assay to RNA and join all the layers
2) Delete all previous SCT assays
3) Rerun SCT on the entire object

I was worried that this would lose the UMAP embeddings, but it appears that those are still intact.

DefaultAssay(SO) <- "RNA"

SO <- JoinLayers(SO)

SO[["SCT"]] <- NULL

SO <- SCTransform(SO)
## Running SCTransform on assay: RNA
## Running SCTransform on layer: counts
## vst.flavor='v2' set. Using model with fixed slope and excluding poisson genes.
## Variance stabilizing transformation of count matrix of size 25651 by 15574
## Model formula is y ~ log_umi
## Get Negative Binomial regression parameters per gene
## Using 2000 genes, 5000 cells
## There are 129 estimated thetas smaller than 1e-07 - will be set to 1e-07
## Found 2 outliers - those will be ignored in fitting/regularization step
## Second step: Get residuals using fitted parameters for 25651 genes
## Computing corrected count matrix for 25651 genes
## Calculating gene attributes
## Wall clock passed: Time difference of 3.388889 mins
## Determine variable features
## Centering data matrix
## Getting residuals for block 1(of 4) for counts dataset
## Getting residuals for block 2(of 4) for counts dataset
## Getting residuals for block 3(of 4) for counts dataset
## Getting residuals for block 4(of 4) for counts dataset
## Centering data matrix
## Finished calculating residuals for counts
## Set default assay to SCT
DimPlot(SO)
